The LCF 5900 course introduces open and accessible science: tools, software and databases that let other researchers access and reproduce your work. For the course I built three fully reproducible projects. Each one has open data, open code, a rendered report and a version you can **run in the browser** with Posit Cloud or Google Colab, with no installation needed.

[[]{.bi .bi-mortarboard} Course page (DokuWiki)](https://guarani.esalq.usp.br/doku.php?id=opensci:2026:alunos:ricardo){.btn-pill .solid}

## Climate of Piracicaba and ENSO

How do long-term seasonal trends in temperature range and rainfall behave in Piracicaba since 1950, and how do El Niño / La Niña anomalies affect extreme local weather, especially summer rainfall? The workflow covers data extraction, exploratory analysis, Kruskal-Wallis tests, Spearman correlation, and forecasting of the Oceanic Niño Index (ONI) with ARIMA and Prophet.

## MAGIC common bean: reproducing a published analysis

Can a published genetics study be reproduced from its open data alone? I re-created the phenotypic and genotypic analyses of a MAGIC (Multiparent Advanced Generation Intercross) population of common bean (*Phaseolus vulgaris* L.) evaluated under drought, to show in practice that scientific reproducibility is feasible.

## Wheat breeding with Bayesian models and information theory

A reproducible pipeline for G×E in rainfed wheat trials. Bayesian hierarchical mixed models handle a 4×4 lattice design and missing data. Mutual information maps non-linear environmental networks and supports multi-trait selection, and Shannon entropy measures phenotypic stability as informational predictability. The result turns raw trial data into decision-support indicators without arbitrary index weights.
